Subject: Commercial exception request: NovaPulse (RP-2026-0471)

Team —

Quick summary: NovaPulse (Series B healthcare analytics startup) is asking for a commercial exception so they can run in two additional US regions (us-west + us-east) and get a one-time credit to offset data egress/transit during their onboarding PoC. They’re also pushing for a lower 12‑month ARR commitment vs our standard 24‑month packaging for Dedicated.

What they’re asking:
- 30% discount on list for the first 12 months (applied to compute + inference units)
- One-time $40k regional onboarding credit (applied as invoiced credit)
- 12‑month term with a 60% commit of estimated sustained usage (instead of 24 months)

Current commercial: initial SOW v3 attached; pricing_workup attached with model/unit math and margin sensitivity. Sales ask: escalate to VP/CFO for exception authority — this will set a precedent for regional credits on multi-region onboardings.

Immediate asks:
1) Marissa: do we have precedent to authorize the $40k credit and shortened term without exec sign-off?
2) Sean/Karthik: any packaging/alternate structures that preserve unit economics (credits applied across first 90 days vs lump sum)?

I’m pushing to keep NovaPulse as a reference for multi-region healthcare customers; if we can’t be flexible they’ll likely go to a cloud vendor. Hoping to move quickly — they’ve signaled urgency for legal and procurement next week.

Thanks,
Vanessa
--
Vanessa Ortiz

Subject: Re: Commercial exception request: NovaPulse (RP-2026-0471)

Vanessa — thanks for the context and the attachments. Quick notes after reviewing pricing_workup:

- $40k onboarding credit as a one-time invoice credit is acceptable operationally, but I need to see the churn/usage ramp assumptions tightened. If their ramp to sustained usage is slower than projected, unit economics go negative.
- 30% off list across compute+inference for 12 months is steeper than our standard practice; recommend capping at 25% with a clear MTU (monthly token usage) milestone tied to the credit clawback.
- Shortening the committed term to 12 months: we can consider it only if they commit to an irrevocable consumption threshold (60% of our modeled baseline) and provide a partial upfront payment (30% of first-year committed ARR) to mitigate churn risk.

If you want an internal sign-off memo for VP/CFO, I can draft one outlining the revised structure (25% discount, $40k credit, 12-month term with 30% upfront and milestone clauses). Otherwise, we’ll need explicit VP sign-off to go to 30%/no upfront.

Marissa

Subject: Re: Commercial exception request: NovaPulse (RP-2026-0471)

Agree with Marissa. A couple pragmatic options to present to the customer that preserve higher realized yield: 

- Option A (preferred): 25% off first 12 months, $40k onboarding credit applied over Q1 invoice schedule (e.g., $13.3k/month for first 3 months), 12-month term, 30% upfront. Credit clawback if monthly usage < 50% of ramp target after month 3.
- Option B (accelerated upsell): 30% off but for first 6 months only; months 7–12 revert to 15% off list. Require 20% upfront.
- Option C (packaging tweak): Keep 24-month term but offer a one-time regional add-on credit (smaller, $25k) and a lower initial discount (20%). This maintains longer term revenue visibility.

I’d recommend presenting A and C to the customer — gives them choice and reduces precedent risk.

—Sean
